title: Double check valve leaking: identify the assembly and leak location
description: Double-check leakage must be located before a repair choice is made.
prompt: Is water leaving a test cock, cover, shutoff, check area, or connected pipe?
answer: Double-check leakage must be located before a repair choice is made. The external point of water does not by itself prove an internal check failure, and the exact assembly controls any service kit path.
urgency: Escalate body damage, failed isolation, high-hazard uncertainty, or a leak that cannot be safely contained.
identifiers: Identify the assembly by label and nominal size, not the phrase double check.
Record the external leak location and any test result separately.
A change in protection type is an authority decision, not a leak repair choice.

choices.label: I know the model and size
choices.detail: Use model-specific sources before ordering parts or accepting a repair scope.

choices.label: The assembly is leaking or failed
choices.detail: Document the location and obtain a qualified diagnosis before repair.

choices.label: The body may be damaged
choices.detail: Compare repair with a complete replacement and retest scope.

steps.title: Observe and identify
steps.body: Photograph the full assembly and specific leak point.

steps.title: Match the verified path
steps.body: Use a qualified diagnosis and model-specific information to distinguish internal and external scope.

steps.title: Close the risk loop
steps.body: Complete required retest and filing after a repair affecting a regulated assembly.

safeChecks: Do not tighten or cap components to conceal leakage.
Keep access to shutoffs and test cocks clear.
Preserve the failed test report if one exists.
stopConditions: The body or connected pipe is cracked.
notThisDevice: A product-family name alone does not establish component compatibility.
A generic online part listing is not a repair diagnosis.
This page does not replace a qualified on-site assessment.
evidenceNote: Use exact manufacturer literature and the governing utility or authority record to validate the device, service path, and compliance closeout.
